Let $n\ge3$ be an integer, let $p,q>0$, and let $A,B>-2$. There is no pair $$u,v\in C^2(\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\})\cap C(\mathbb R^n), \qquad u(x)>0,\quad v(x)>0\quad(x\in\mathbb R^n),$$ satisfying Equation [eq:system] at every $x\ne0$ if and only if $$\frac{n+A}{p+1}+\frac{n+B}{q+1}>n-2.$$ When the reverse weak inequality holds, such a pair exists and can be chosen radial.
